title: A Spire for the Wolf
premise: Noor Thackeray keeps the ledgers of the Mnemosyne Guild, which trades bottled memories to nobles desperate to forget or remember. When a dying courier forces a map of the Sunken Spire into her hands and dies whispering her true name—a name she never knew she had—Noor becomes hunted by the Guild's master, Vess Corvane, who wants the map to wake the slumbering god-wolf beneath the city. Along the way Noor gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced lamplighter, a memory-eater child, and the ghost of the courier trapped in her own mind. In the Spire, Noor learns she is the last vessel of the wolf's stolen memory, and rather than let Corvane weaponize it or destroy it, she releases it into the world, ending her invisibility but claiming her identity at last.
about_author: Orsen Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction about the things we refuse to remember. They write in a drafty tower room and claim, unconvincingly, to have never stolen anything.

chapters.title: The Weight of Other People's Yesterdays
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the Guild's candlelit counting room, Noor catalogs bottled memories and quietly pockets a vial of a mother's lullaby she can't explain wanting. Establishes her invisibility, her ledgers, and her loneliness. Emotional beat: aching yearning beneath practiced detachment.

chapters.title: The Courier at the Door
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses into her lodgings, presses a wax-sealed map into her hands, and dies saying a name Noor has never heard but somehow recognizes. She hides the body and the map, terrified. Emotional beat: shock cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the Guild, Master Vess Corvane questions her too gently about a missing courier. Noor lies for the first time in years and realizes he already suspects. Emotional beat: dread wearing the mask of routine.

chapters.title: The Lamplighter's Debt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Disgraced lamplighter Sable Quinn, who once sold a decade of his own memories to the Guild, spots Noor fleeing through the undercity and offers help to repay an old debt he can't remember incurring. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: A Name in the Dark
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The map shows the Sunken Spire and a route through the drowned quarter. The courier's ghost begins speaking to Noor from inside her mind, calling her by the stranger's name. Emotional beat: identity beginning to surface like a drowned thing.

chapters.title: The Memory-Eater
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They shelter with Pip, a feral child who eats memories whole and remembers nothing, including how she came to the undercity. Pip imprints on Noor, sensing a memory inside her that isn't hers. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: What Corvane Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor breaks into Corvane's private vault and finds centuries of ledgers—and a vial labeled with her unknown name, dated before her birth. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering your life was written by another hand.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corvane's Retrievers raid the undercity. Sable and Pip are nearly taken; Sable burns his last unspent memory to buy their escape, forgetting something precious. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the price of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Drowned Quarter
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The three descend into the flooded ruins beneath the city, guided by the ghost and the map. Noor confesses she doesn't know who she is; Sable says neither does he, and it's fine. Emotional beat: found family solidifying in the dark.

chapters.title: The Wolf Beneath the Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They reach the Spire's outer gate, where ancient wards read Noor's blood and open. The ghost reveals the wolf god's memory was stolen and hidden in a human vessel—her. Emotional beat: terror of being the answer to an old war.

chapters.title: Pip Remembers
chapters.summary: Pip's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. Pip tastes the air of the Spire and suddenly remembers everything she's ever eaten, including a fragment of the wolf's memory: a war, a betrayal by the Guild's founders. Emotional beat: a child carrying a god's grief.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corvane and his Retrievers breach the drowned quarter. Sable stays behind to hold a collapsing gate, buying time, and is captured. Emotional beat: courage without hope of thanks.

chapters.title: The Stolen Century
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Inside the Spire, the ghost shows Noor the truth: the Guild was founded to guard the wolf's memory, then corrupted. Corvane intends to feed the memory to the city's elites and rule the waking god. Emotional beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The courier's ghost asks to be released once the wolf's memory is free; Noor promises. The ghost warns the memory will burn out any vessel that releases it. Emotional beat: acceptance of a possible death.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Imprisoned, Sable bargains with a sympathetic Retriever, trading the last scraps of his forgotten past for a message smuggled to Noor. Emotional beat: love expressed through loss.

chapters.title: What Noor Thackeray Forgot
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor unlocks her own sealed memories: she was made, not born—a vessel raised by the Guild, her childhood a fabrication, her name a cage. Emotional beat: grief and liberation entangled.

chapters.title: The Spire Wakes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Corvane arrives with Sable as hostage and forces Noor to the heart of the Spire. The wolf's memory stirs; the city above begins to shake. Pip arrives, wild and remembering. Emotional beat: everything converging.

chapters.title: The Choice of Vessels
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. Corvane demands the memory; Noor refuses to give it to him or destroy it. Instead she begins releasing it—not into the wolf, but into the world, into everyone, so no one can own it. The ghost departs, freed. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as self-definition.

chapters.title: Everything the Light Touches Remembers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, climax continued. The memory disperses through the city; citizens wake with fragments of the wolf's grief and wonder. Corvane, denied a monopoly, is unmade by the very memory he sought. Sable and Pip reach Noor's side as the Spire crumbles. Emotional beat: awe and release.

chapters.title: After the Falling
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The city survives, changed; the Guild's ledgers are opened to the public. Sable and Pip dig Noor from the rubble, alive but emptied of the wolf's memory and her own fabricated past. Emotional beat: exhaustion and fierce relief.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor, with no history but the one she'll write, opens a small shop that returns stolen memories to their owners for free. Pip stays; Sable stays. Emotional beat: quiet joy of a chosen family.

chapters.title: The Wolf in the Window
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. On the first anniversary, a great wolf-shaped shadow passes the shop window, pauses, and moves on—free, unowned, remembering. Noor smiles and writes a new name in a fresh ledger: her own. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, to oneself.
